texts: Compared with surgical aortic valve replacement in intermediate-risk patients, transcatheter replacement has a higher rate of significant paravalvular leak.
A transcatheter valve is pressed against a calcified annulus rather than sewn in, so gaps can remain around its edge, and even moderate leak is linked to higher late mortality.
Surgical replacement has higher rates of acute kidney injury, major bleeding and new atrial fibrillation (PARTNER 2A, SURTAVI).
Newer valves with outer skirts have reduced the difference in leak but not removed it.
In the picture, the folded dentures leak round their edges, while the sewn dentures are tight but bring the kidney beans, the dripping tap and Pinocchio.
Memory hook: folded dentures leak at the edges; sewn ones bleed and flutter.
